column1: # WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `core/db/migrations/*` was globbed to canon-recording, on the reasoning that a
# migration is a schema change. That is true and it is not enough: 56 of these 64 migrations are not
# primarily canon-recording work. The proof was that 28 feature stems had their migration in one area
# and their own test in another — 20260807100003_journey.sql owned by canon-recording while
# A path glob cannot see what a migration is FOR. So each migration declares it, the same way a Go file
# declares its ADR with `Governed-by:` rather than being matched by a hand-written path map — the map
# that covered 231 of 322 files and failed by being quiet (core/api/governance_test.go:11-25).
# canon-recording is a CO-OWNER OF EVERY ROW HERE and is not repeated below. Every migration is a
# change to the Master DDL surface and must satisfy D-4, append-only (B-5/ADR-006), `make schema-check`,
# and replay (I-1). The area named below is the SECOND owner: whose feature this serves. Both experts
# Applied migration files are never edited to carry this — a sidecar cannot change a checksum or a
# schema dump. `harness/check.sh areas` asserts completeness BOTH WAYS: a migration with no row here
# fails, and a row here naming no migration fails. So it cannot drift.
